$comment: Which status checks are INTENDED to block a merge to main (#1559).
This file is the in-repo source of truth. It exists because the guard that
validates branch protection could only read the live ruleset through an
admin-scoped GitHub API call, which the CI token cannot make — so it skipped
on every run and validated nothing. Declaring intent here lets the guard do
its most important job (every required context has a producing job) with no
API access at all, and treat the live ruleset as drift detection on top.
`required` must match the contexts in the active 'Branch Protection' ruleset.
Each entry must equal a job `name:` in .github/workflows/*.yml exactly —
renaming a job is a breaking change to branch protection (#1561).
`advisory` records checks that deliberately run without blocking merge, so a
reader is not misled into thinking they gate anything.

advisory.reason: Runs the ratcheting audit gate and can fail, but is not in the ruleset, so a new advisory does not block merge. Promoting it is tracked separately — see #1559.
workflow_dispatch + weekly schedule only; never runs on a pull request, so it cannot be a required context.
Separate check-migrations.yml workflow. Overlaps the required 'Check Migrations' job in ci.yml.
